誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券)
參加者納入標準：
18
至
29
歲
在香港居住的本地年輕成人
在過去
18
個月內經歷過親友
/
重要的人離世
能閱懂中文和以廣東話溝通
研究程序：
1
）基線問卷
填妥同意書後，參加者將完成一份20分鐘基線問卷
問卷問題將與面對及經歷親友/重要的人離世時的哀傷過程及對死亡的觀念有關
完成基線問卷將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
2
）第一輪跟進問卷
六個月後，我們會邀請參加者完成一份跟進問卷
完成第一輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
3
）第二輪跟進問卷
在完成第一輪跟進問卷的六個月後，我們會邀請參加者再次完成一份跟進問卷
完成第二輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
本研究均屬自願參與。研究資料會被保密，除研究人員外，任何人均不能獲取參與者所填寫的問卷資訊或錄音內容。本研究已通過香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會(CREC-2025.748)及香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理(SBRE‐24‐0378)審查。
參加方法:
請用以下連結填寫同意書及問卷，完成後可獲送贈港幣
一百元
正超市禮券
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊合資格的香港年輕成人。
如有查詢，請與博士後研究員凌皓峰博士聯絡。
電郵: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp: 44643831

WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk

Professional Certificate in Mindfulness Facilitator Training Programme(Apply by 16 Nov 2026!)  - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Emily Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
emilyleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Integrating Mindfulness into Professional Practice: A Mindfulness Facilitator Training
Are you a professional in healthcare, social work, psychology, or education who wants to integrate mindfulness into your service, but feels unsure about how to introduce it safely and flexibly?
Many frontline practitioners have learned approaches that incorporate mindfulness (such as ACT or DBT), but due to limited course hours, may feel their core grasp of mindfulness needs a deeper, more solid foundation.
Taught in Cantonese, this training is designed specifically for professionals working with adult service users. It moves beyond standard 8-week group training to focus on practical 1-on-1 applications, short workshops, and experiential creative tools!
3 Programme Highlights:
Creative & Diverse Modalities: Go beyond foundational practices with Mindful Tea Drinking, Mindful Clay, and Mindful Jar creation—engaging ways to introduce mindfulness to your clients.
Tailored for Helping Contexts: Learn to guide mindfulness safely, ethically, and adaptively within individual counseling or group sessions.
Comprehensive Support System: Includes 6 months of structured learning, a 3-day silent retreat, small-group tutorials, and post-course practice supervision.
Trainer: Prof. Stanley Chan
• Adjunct Assistant Professor, JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
• Educational Psychologist (HKDEP Registered)
• Oxford Mindfulness Foundation (OMF) Certified Trainer
• Mindfulness Network (UK) Approved Supervisor
Course Schedule & Logistics
Stage 1: Theory & Core Skills (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
Dec 19, 2026 (Sat) | Jan 2, Jan 16, Jan 30, Jan 31 (Sun), Feb 13, 2027 (Sat)
• 1st Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): March 7, 2027 (Sun)
Stage 2: 3-Day Silent Retreat (Non-overnight, Venue TBC)
• Full-Day Retreat (09:30 – 18:30 TBC): March 26–28, 2027 (Easter Holiday, Fri–Sun)
• 2nd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): April 10, 2027 (Sat)
Stage 3: Practice & Integration (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
April 24, May 1, May 8, 2027 (Sat)
• 3rd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): May 22 & May 29, 2027 (mornings)
Post-Course Supervision Stage:
• 2 sessions of small group practice supervision (1.5 hrs each) within 30–90 days following Stage 3.
Entry Requirements:
1. Mindfulness Foundation: Completion of an 8-week mindfulness course (MBCT, MBCT-L, or MBSR) by an accredited organization/teacher.
2. Professional Qualification: Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, health, or social services with active membership in a regulated local professional body (e.g., Registered Social Worker, Educational/Clinical Psychologist, Registered Nurse).
3. Silent Retreat Experience: Completion of one 5-7 day or two 3-day overnight silent retreats. (Note: Applicants currently pending retreat completion may still apply provided they commit to fulfilling it before completing this training.)
Fees:
• Application Fee: HKD $300
• Tuition Fee: HKD $29,500
Application Deadline: 16 November 2026 (Admissions on a rolling basis—early submission is strongly encouraged!)
Learn More & Apply Online:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13743848
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
[CUHK AIoT Lab] Hiring Undergraduate Student Helpers — Design & Promotion / Outreach & Real-World Practice / Data Pipeline 【CUHK AIoT Lab 招募本科生 Student Helper】宣傳設計 · 對外交流 · 數據 Pipeline - Information Engineering
From: Alex, Xinyan Wang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
alex.wang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【CUHK AIoT Lab 招募本科生 Student Helper】宣傳設計 · 對外交流 · 數據 Pipeline
我們是香港中文大學訊息工程學系 AIoT Lab，由邢國良教授（Prof. Guoliang Xing）領導，專注 AI + IoT + Healthcare 前沿研究。實驗室正在推進的 AD2025 家居健康感知項目已完成 190+ 戶長者家庭部署（覆蓋香港十八區）；團隊同時開展學術工作坊、數據集對外授權、產學合作與初創孵化。
■ 關於實驗室
• 邢國良教授為 ACM Fellow（2024）及 IEEE Fellow（2020），並於 2025 年獲選香港研資局高級研究學者（RGC Senior Research Fellow，全港各學科僅 10 人）。
• 於 MobiCom、MobiSys、IPSN、ICNP 等國際頂級學術會議合共獲 6 項最佳論文獎，最新為 MobiCom 2025 最佳論文獎；並於 2024、2025 連續兩屆日內瓦國際發明展奪得金獎。
• 近 5 年累積科研經費逾 8,000 萬港幣，包括一項 3,900 萬港幣的 RGC 大型資助（2025–2030，基礎模型 × 老年退化性疾病早期診斷與干預）。
• 研究成果發表於 MobiCom、MobiSys、SenSys、SIGCOMM、NeurIPS 等頂級國際會議及期刊；多項技術獲工業界採用，並獲 Google 等國際頂尖 AI 機構主動接洽真實場景數據合作。
• 研究成果已孵化出機器人與真實場景數據方向的初創公司。
• 實驗室學生曾入選福布斯中國 30 Under 30，畢業生於 HKUST 等知名學府任教；實驗室配備 GPU 叢集、邊緣計算平台及 Unitree 人形機器人等研發設施。
■ 現誠聘本科生 Student Helper，設以下三個方向（可同時申請多於一個）：
■ 方向一：宣傳 / 設計 / 營運
工作內容：
• 為研究項目及實驗室活動（工作坊、Info Day、講座等）設計海報、簡報及社交媒體圖文
• 撰寫並維護中英文宣傳內容（網站、社交平台）
• 協助活動策劃、現場執行與回顧整理
我們希望你：
• 有設計經驗或興趣皆可（Figma / Canva / Adobe 或任何順手的工具），有影片剪輯經驗更佳；作品集非必須，如有可附上
• 具備基礎中英文書寫能力
• 對科技傳播與視覺敘事有興趣
■ 方向二：對外交流 / 落地實踐（Pitch & Outreach）
工作內容：
• 協助撰寫及製作 pitch deck、計劃書與對外展示材料
• 支援數據集對外授權、產學合作及孵化初創的對外洽談與跟進
• 協助對外聯絡與接待（企業、投資人、媒體、來訪者）
• 協助活動策劃及會議組織
我們希望你：
• 對科研成果落地、pitch、對外交流感興趣，樂於與人打交道
• 具備基礎中英文溝通能力，願意學習製作簡報
• 做事有條理、細心、可靠
■ 方向三：數據 Pipeline
工作內容：
• 開發及維護多模態感知數據（深度、音訊、影片）處理 pipeline
• 數據清洗、質檢（QC）、去識別化、打包及版本管理
• 支撐數據集公開發布與研究平台迭代
我們希望你：
• 有 Python 基礎即可，用過 Linux 命令行更佳；Git / Docker 經驗優先
• 細心負責，對數據工程感興趣
• 無需研究經驗，我們提供培訓與指引
■ 基本要求
• CUHK 全日制本科生，專業不限（設計、商科、理工背景均歡迎）
• 對科技內容有興趣者優先：我們的工作圍繞 AI、機器人、健康科技等前沿科技展開
• 工作地點：中大校園；部分任務可遠端進行
• 可長期參與（至少一學年）者優先
■ 你可以獲得
• 深度參與真實推進的 AI + Healthcare 研究項目及其成果發布
• 在真實場景中累積 pitch、對外洽談或數據工程經驗（視乎方向）
• 與 ACM/IEEE Fellow 團隊及博士生緊密合作
• 表現優秀者可獲推薦信並深入參與研究——歷屆 helper 中有人赴 HKU 攻讀 MPhil、有人成為中大 PhD 學生（HKPFS 得主）
■ 申請方式
請聯絡 Alex（Email: alex.wang@link.cuhk.edu.hk | WhatsApp: 54448449），並提供：
• 姓名 / 年級 / 專業
• 申請方向（可多選）
• 每週可工作時段
• 相關經驗或興趣介紹（作品集非必須，如有可附上）
期待你的加入！
────────────────────────────────────────
[CUHK AIoT Lab] Hiring Undergraduate Student Helpers — Design & Promotion / Outreach & Real-World Practice / Data Pipeline
We are the AIoT Lab in the Department of Information Engineering at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), led by Prof. Guoliang Xing, focusing on AI + IoT + Healthcare. Our in-home health sensing project (AD2025) has completed deployments in 190+ elderly households across all 18 districts of Hong Kong. The lab also runs academic workshops, dataset licensing, industry collaborations, and startup incubation.
■ About the Lab
• Prof. Guoliang Xing is an ACM Fellow (2024) and IEEE Fellow (2020), and was named an RGC Senior Research Fellow in 2025 — one of only 10 recipients across all disciplines in Hong Kong.
• Our work has earned 6 Best Paper Awards at top international conferences including MobiCom, MobiSys, IPSN and ICNP — most recently the MobiCom 2025 Best Paper Award — plus Gold Medals at the Geneva International Exhibition of Inventions in both 2024 and 2025.
• Over the past five years, the lab has secured HK$80M+ in research funding, including a HK$39M RGC grant (2025–2030) on foundation models for early diagnosis and intervention of aging-related degenerative diseases.
• Our research is published at top international conferences and journals including MobiCom, MobiSys, SenSys, SIGCOMM and NeurIPS; several technologies have been adopted by industry, and leading global AI organizations such as Google have approached us for real-world data collaborations.
• Our research has already spun off a startup in robotics and real-world data.
• Our students have been named to Forbes China 30 Under 30, and our graduates hold faculty positions at leading universities such as HKUST. The lab is equipped with GPU clusters, edge computing platforms, and a Unitree humanoid robot.
■ We are now recruiting undergraduate Student Helpers in three tracks (you may apply for more than one):
■ Track 1: Promotion / Design / Operations
What you'll do:
• Design posters, slides, and social media graphics for our research projects and events (workshops, info days, seminars)
• Write and maintain bilingual (Chinese/English) content for our website and social channels
• Help plan, run, and document lab events
We're looking for someone who:
• Has design experience, or simply a genuine interest in design (Figma / Canva / Adobe or any tools you're comfortable with); video editing is a plus — a portfolio is welcome but not required
• Has basic writing skills in Chinese and English
• Is interested in science communication and visual storytelling
■ Track 2: Outreach & Real-World Practice (Pitch & External Communications)
What you'll do:
• Help prepare pitch decks, project plans, and external-facing presentation materials
• Support external discussions and follow-ups for dataset licensing, industry partnerships, and our spin-off's outreach activities
• Assist with external outreach and reception (companies, investors, media, visitors)
• Help plan events and organize meetings
We're looking for someone who:
• Is interested in bringing research into real-world practice, pitching, and outreach, and enjoys meeting people
• Has basic communication skills in Chinese and English; happy to learn presentation-making
• Is well-organized, detail-oriented, and reliable
■ Track 3: Data Pipeline
What you'll do:
• Build and maintain data processing pipelines for multimodal sensing data (depth, audio, video)
• Handle data cleaning, QC, de-identification, packaging, and versioning
• Support public dataset releases and research platform iterations
We're looking for someone who:
• Has basic Python skills — that's enough; some Linux command-line experience helps, and Git / Docker experience is a plus
• Is careful, responsible, and interested in data engineering
• No prior research experience required — we provide training and guidance
■ Requirements
• Full-time CUHK undergraduates; all majors welcome (design, business, and STEM backgrounds are all encouraged)
• Interest in technology is strongly preferred: our work revolves around frontier topics such as AI, robotics, and health tech
• Location: CUHK campus; some tasks can be done remotely
• Long-term availability (one academic year or more) preferred
■ What you'll gain
• Hands-on involvement in a live AI + Healthcare research project and its public releases
• Real-world practice in pitching, external meetings, or data engineering, depending on your track
• Close collaboration with an ACM/IEEE Fellow's team and PhD researchers
• Strong performers may receive recommendation letters and deeper research involvement — past helpers have gone on to an MPhil at HKU and PhD studies at CUHK (including an HKPFS awardee)
■ How to apply
Contact Alex (Email: alex.wang@link.cuhk.edu.hk | WhatsApp: 54448449) with:
• Your name / year of study / major
• The track(s) you're applying for
• Your weekly availability
• Relevant experience or interests (a portfolio is optional — attach one if you have it)
We look forward to hearing from you!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

• 對科技傳播與視覺敘事有興趣
■ 方向二：對外交流 / 落地實踐（Pitch & Outreach）
工作內容：
• 協助撰寫及製作 pitch deck、計劃書與對外展示材料
• 支援數據集對外授權、產學合作及孵化初創的對外洽談與跟進
• 協助對外聯絡與接待（企業、投資人、媒體、來訪者）
• 協助活動策劃及會議組織
我們希望你：
• 對科研成果落地、pitch、對外交流感興趣，樂於與人打交道
• 具備基礎中英文溝通能力，願意學習製作簡報
• 做事有條理、細心、可靠
■ 方向三：數據 Pipeline
工作內容：
• 開發及維護多模態感知數據（深度、音訊、影片）處理 pipeline
• 數據清洗、質檢（QC）、去識別化、打包及版本管理
• 支撐數據集公開發布與研究平台迭代
我們希望你：
• 有 Python 基礎即可，用過 Linux 命令行更佳；Git / Docker 經驗優先
• 細心負責，對數據工程感興趣
• 無需研究經驗，我們提供培訓與指引
■ 基本要求
• CUHK 全日制本科生，專業不限（設計、商科、理工背景均歡迎）
• 對科技內容有興趣者優先：我們的工作圍繞 AI、機器人、健康科技等前沿科技展開
• 工作地點：中大校園；部分任務可遠端進行
• 可長期參與（至少一學年）者優先
■ 你可以獲得
• 深度參與真實推進的 AI + Healthcare 研究項目及其成果發布
• 在真實場景中累積 pitch、對外洽談或數據工程經驗（視乎方向）
• 與 ACM/IEEE Fellow 團隊及博士生緊密合作
• 表現優秀者可獲推薦信並深入參與研究——歷屆 helper 中有人赴 HKU 攻讀 MPhil、有人成為中大 PhD 學生（HKPFS 得主）
■ 申請方式
請聯絡 Alex（Email: alex.wang@link.cuhk.edu.hk | WhatsApp: 54448449），並提供：
• 姓名 / 年級 / 專業
• 申請方向（可多選）
• 每週可工作時段
• 相關經驗或興趣介紹（作品集非必須，如有可附上）
期待你的加入！
────────────────────────────────────────
[CUHK AIoT Lab] Hiring Undergraduate Student Helpers — Design & Promotion / Outreach & Real-World Practice / Data Pipeline
We are the AIoT Lab in the Department of Information Engineering at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), led by Prof. Guoliang Xing, focusing on AI + IoT + Healthcare. Our in-home health sensing project (AD2025) has completed deployments in 190+ elderly households across all 18 districts of Hong Kong. The lab also runs academic workshops, dataset licensing, industry collaborations, and startup incubation.
■ About the Lab
• Prof. Guoliang Xing is an ACM Fellow (2024) and IEEE Fellow (2020), and was named an RGC Senior Research Fellow in 2025 — one of only 10 recipients across all disciplines in Hong Kong.
• Our work has earned 6 Best Paper Awards at top international conferences including MobiCom, MobiSys, IPSN and ICNP — most recently the MobiCom 2025 Best Paper Award — plus Gold Medals at the Geneva International Exhibition of Inventions in both 2024 and 2025.
• Over the past five years, the lab has secured HK$80M+ in research funding, including a HK$39M RGC grant (2025–2030) on foundation models for early diagnosis and intervention of aging-related degenerative diseases.
• Our research is published at top international conferences and journals including MobiCom, MobiSys, SenSys, SIGCOMM and NeurIPS; several technologies have been adopted by industry, and leading global AI organizations such as Google have approached us for real-world data collaborations.
• Our research has already spun off a startup in robotics and real-world data.
• Our students have been named to Forbes China 30 Under 30, and our graduates hold faculty positions at leading universities such as HKUST. The lab is equipped with GPU clusters, edge computing platforms, and a Unitree humanoid robot.
■ We are now recruiting undergraduate Student Helpers in three tracks (you may apply for more than one):
■ Track 1: Promotion / Design / Operations
What you'll do:
• Design posters, slides, and social media graphics for our research projects and events (workshops, info days, seminars)
• Write and maintain bilingual (Chinese/English) content for our website and social channels
• Help plan, run, and document lab events
We're looking for someone who:
• Has design experience, or simply a genuine interest in design (Figma / Canva / Adobe or any tools you're comfortable with); video editing is a plus — a portfolio is welcome but not required
• Has basic writing skills in Chinese and English
• Is interested in science communication and visual storytelling
■ Track 2: Outreach & Real-World Practice (Pitch & External Communications)
What you'll do:
• Help prepare pitch decks, project plans, and external-facing presentation materials
• Support external discussions and follow-ups for dataset licensing, industry partnerships, and our spin-off's outreach activities
• Assist with external outreach and reception (companies, investors, media, visitors)
• Help plan events and organize meetings
We're looking for someone who:
• Is interested in bringing research into real-world practice, pitching, and outreach, and enjoys meeting people
• Has basic communication skills in Chinese and English; happy to learn presentation-making
• Is well-organized, detail-oriented, and reliable
■ Track 3: Data Pipeline
What you'll do:
• Build and maintain data processing pipelines for multimodal sensing data (depth, audio, video)
• Handle data cleaning, QC, de-identification, packaging, and versioning
• Support public dataset releases and research platform iterations
We're looking for someone who:
• Has basic Python skills — that's enough; some Linux command-line experience helps, and Git / Docker experience is a plus
• Is careful, responsible, and interested in data engineering
• No prior research experience required — we provide training and guidance
■ Requirements
• Full-time CUHK undergraduates; all majors welcome (design, business, and STEM backgrounds are all encouraged)
• Interest in technology is strongly preferred: our work revolves around frontier topics such as AI, robotics, and health tech
• Location: CUHK campus; some tasks can be done remotely
• Long-term availability (one academic year or more) preferred
■ What you'll gain
• Hands-on involvement in a live AI + Healthcare research project and its public releases
• Real-world practice in pitching, external meetings, or data engineering, depending on your track
• Close collaboration with an ACM/IEEE Fellow's team and PhD researchers
• Strong performers may receive recommendation letters and deeper research involvement — past helpers have gone on to an MPhil at HKU and PhD studies at CUHK (including an HKPFS awardee)
■ How to apply
Contact Alex (Email: alex.wang@link.cuhk.edu.hk | WhatsApp: 54448449) with:
• Your name / year of study / major
• The track(s) you're applying for
• Your weekly availability
• Relevant experience or interests (a portfolio is optional — attach one if you have it)
We look forward to hearing from you!
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Chen Zhuolin
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
dorinchen@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Colleagues and Students,
You and your family members are cordially invited to participate in the upcoming "Silver Age Smart Dressing & Fashion Show" (銀齡智慧穿搭秀).
As the weather changes, dressing smartly keeps us warm, safe, and confident. Through this three-part programme, participants will learn how to create stylish, comfortable, and safe winter outfits using their own everyday wardrobe. No new clothes needed!
Activity Highlights
No need to purchase new clothing: Style brand-new looks using your everyday personal wardrobe!
Expert tips: Learn flexible thermal layering to stay warm, ditch bulky clothing, and move safely.
Rewards & prizes: Supermarket vouchers and multiple attractive awards will be presented to participants!
Programme Schedule (Three Sessions)
Session 1: Lecture & Briefing Session
Date & Time: 21 November 2026 (Saturday) | 10:00 – 12:00
Venue: Zone F, 1/F, Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building, CUHK
Session 2: Group Follow-up & Practice
Date & Time: 30 November 2026 (Monday) | 10:00 – 12:00
Venue: Zone C, 1/F, Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building, CUHK
Session 3: Smart Dressing Fashion Show
Date & Time: 12 December 2026 (Saturday) | 10:00 – 12:00
Venue: G03, Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building, CUHK
Eligibility & Quota
Target Participants: Older adults aged 60 or above
Quota: 30 participants
Registration & Enquiries
Online Registration:
https://forms.gle/VtShgC7hvm2BM1L17
Telephone Registration / Enquiry: 3943 4168 (Office Hours)
Registration Deadline: 18 November 2026 (Wednesday)
各位教職員及同學：
誠邀閣下及長輩參與由香港中文大學及香港大學聯合主辦的「銀齡智慧穿搭秀」系列活動！
天氣多變，點著最掂？活動透過三部曲工作坊及時裝秀，由專家指導靈活保暖技巧，毋須額外添置新衣，運用日常私伙衣物即可展現個人風格與活力，兼顧保暖、時尚、自信與健康！
活動亮點
毋須買新衫： 運用日常私伙衣物，穿出全新個人風格！
專家指導： 教授靈活式保暖穿搭技巧，告別臃腫，行動更安全！
豐富獎品： 設有超市禮券及多個豐富獎項！
活動日程
第一節：講座及簡報會
日期及時間： 2026年11月21日（星期六）上午 10:00 – 12:00
地點： 香港中文大學 李兆基建築學大樓 1樓 Zone F

日期及時間： 2026年11月30日（星期一）上午 10:00 – 12:00
地點： 香港中文大學 李兆基建築學大樓 1樓 Zone C
第三節：智慧穿搭時裝秀
日期及時間： 2026年12月12日（星期六）上午 10:00 – 12:00
地點： 香港中文大學 李兆基建築學大樓 G03
對象及名額
參加對象： 60歲或以上長者
名額： 30人
報名及查詢
網上報名：
https://forms.gle/VtShgC7hvm2BM1L17
電話登記 / 查詢： 3943 4168（辦公時間）
截止報名日期： 2026年11月18日（星期三）

Announcements
Cantonese / English Native Speakers and Cantonese–English Bilinguals Wanted (HK$67 per hour)  招募英語母語者、粵語母語者及粵英雙語者評估兒童語言研究材料（每小時港幣67元津貼） - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: YANG Wenwen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wenwenyang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學語言學及現代語言系現正進行一項兒童語言研究，招募以下參加者：英語母語者2名，粵語母語者2名，粵英雙語者2名。
不同語言背景的參加者將負責不同的評估：
英語母語者：聆聽英語錄音，評估錄音的清晰度、自然度、發音及整體可接受性。評估任務預計約需一小時。
粵語母語者：聆聽粵語錄音，評估錄音的清晰度、自然度、發音及整體可接受性。評估任務預計約需一小時。
粵英雙語者：比較成對的英文及粵語文本，評估兩個版本在含義、資訊量、語言難度及兒童適宜性方面是否對等。雙語評估者亦可能需要抽聽少量錄音，以確認實際錄音內容與文本一致。評估任務預計約需30分鐘。
所有評估均於網上進行。津貼將按實際完成時間，以每小時港幣67元計算。
參加者條件：年滿18歲；符合上述其中一類語言背景；能夠理解相應語言的日常口語及書面表達；願意按照簡單指引於網上完成評估。
有興趣者請填寫登記表：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1UkBz96b1jizXhQ
合適的登記者將獲聯絡，並收到具體安排。登記表所收集的個人資料只會用於招募、篩選及聯絡，並會保密處理。
如有查詢，請電郵楊雯雯：wenwenyang@cuhk.edu.hk。
The Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting: Two native English speakers; Two native Cantonese speakers; And two Cantonese–English bilinguals.
Participants will complete different tasks according to their language background:
Native English speakers will listen to English recordings and evaluate their clarity, naturalness, pronunciation, and overall acceptability. The evaluation is expected to take approximately one hour.
Native Cantonese speakers will listen to Cantonese recordings and evaluate their clarity, naturalness, pronunciation, and overall acceptability. The evaluation is expected to take approximately one hour.
Cantonese–English bilinguals will compare paired English and Cantonese texts and assess whether they are equivalent in meaning, information content, language difficulty, and suitability for children. They may also be asked to listen to a small selection of recordings to confirm that the recorded content corresponds to the written texts. The evaluation is expected to take approximately 30 minutes.
All evaluations will be conducted online. Participation will be compensated at HK$67 per hour, based on the actual time spent.
Eligibility:
Aged 18 or above;
Belonging to one of the language groups listed above;
Able to understand everyday spoken and written language in the relevant language(s);
Willing to complete the online evaluation following brief instructions.
If you are interested, please complete the registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1UkBz96b1jizXhQ
Suitable applicants will be contacted with further details. Personal information submitted through the registration form will be used only for recruitment, screening, and contact and will be handled confidentially.
For enquiries, please email Wenwen Yang at wenwenyang@cuhk.edu.hk.

From: Whitney Sia

「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，首場講座在 10 月 25 日圓滿結束，第二場講座將於 11 月 28 日繼續在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行，誠邀大家參加！
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。
本講座系列為香港研究資助局協作研究計劃「嶺南文化與世界」項目（2023–2026）活動，亦是弘揚中華文化系列的活動之一。

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries. The first lecture was successfully held on 25 October. The second lecture will take place at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 28 November.
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries. The first lecture was successfully held on 25 October. The second lecture will take place at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 28 November.
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

From: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
spc@lib.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
日期：2026年11月24日（星期二）
時間：09:30–12:30, 14:00–15:30
形式：現場及線上
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地下研討室
語言：普通話
主辦：香港中文大學圖書館、復旦大學圖書館、中華古籍保護研究院
講題一：關於古籍保護與古籍活化幾個問題（09:30–11:00）
古籍是中華文明的重要載體。如何在妥善保護的基礎上推動古籍開放利用，使其更好地服務學術研究、教育教學與公眾文化生活，是高校古籍保護與傳承的重要課題。講座圍繞「古籍活化」主題，結合國內外相關實踐，探討高校古籍資源開放共用、數字化與數字人文研究、古籍保護與整理、人才培養及跨學科合作等問題，並關注傳統技藝展示、校園曝書節、文化體驗與公眾教育等活化方式，思考如何協調保護與利用的關係，拓展古籍傳播途徑，更好地發揮古籍的學術價值與文化價值。
講者簡介：楊光輝教授，復旦大學中華古籍保護研究院/文物保護創新研究院常務副院長，研究館員，文學博士，古籍保護學博士生導師。主要研究方向為古籍保護學、索引學、海外漢學。上海市曙光學者。美國匹茲堡大學、耶魯大學訪問學者，哈佛大學博士後。中國索引學會副理事長兼秘書長，中國古籍保護協會常務理事/傳統寫印材料研究專業委員會主任委員。《薩都剌生平及著作實證研究》獲全國百篇優秀博士學位論文獎。編撰《中國歷代園林圖文精選》（第四輯），翻譯（美）韓南（Patrick Hanan）《The Invention of Li Yu（創造李漁）》。主編《版本目錄學研究》、《中國索引》、《復旦大學圖書館藏詩經文獻叢刊》等。
講題二：中國傳統手工紙制造原理、發展與其他（11:00–12:30）
講座立足傳統書寫載體體系，介紹傳統手工紙的製造原理，點出纖維提取與纖維交織兩個關鍵點。同時討論古法造紙技藝在當代傳承、原料、產業化等方面面臨的現實問題，並針對學界關注的紙張起源問題，辨析史料、考古證據差異，釐清造紙起源的爭議，幫助聽眾建立對傳統造紙技術較為客觀、理性的認知。最後，對古籍保護中的交叉研究問題進行示例。
講者簡介：劉鵬博士，工學博士，復旦大學中華古籍保護研究院副研究員。具有制漿造紙工程和高分子材料學複合背景。主要研究方向聚焦古籍保護與傳統寫印材料科學，深耕古法手工紙墨等傳統文房材料的成分剖析與古法復原，同時開展貝葉經等少數民族古文獻的病害機理研究與科學保護工作。在古籍保護、文博、材料國內外核心期刊發表學術論文二十餘篇，獲授權發明專利八項。在行業與教學領域，主講傳統寫印材料紙張工藝等核心課程，同時參與博士生、碩士生課題指導工作，並開展古籍保護、古法材料覆刻產學研合作。
講題三：紙質文獻保護修復：基礎技法與案例實踐（14:30–15:30）
課程圍繞紙質文獻保護修復的基本方法與實踐操作展開，介紹常見病害調查、修復工具與材料選擇、修復方案制定及檔案記錄。通過示範與實操，講解漿糊製備、補紙選配、傳統手工修補及紙漿補書等技術的操作要點。結合大面積缺損、嚴重蟲蛀、手稿及散葉文獻等典型案例，指導學員開展修復實踐，並學習書葉整理、傳統線裝書裝訂及修復質量檢查等內容，提升學員分析病害、選擇修復方法和實際操作的能力。
講者簡介：李燕女士，復旦大學圖書情報專業碩士，復旦大學圖書館館員、古籍修復師，加拿大不列顛哥倫比亞大學訪問學者，國際「貝葉文獻科學保護與修復」實踐工作坊主講教師。長期從事紙質文獻和貝葉文獻保護修復工作，並開展相關教學、培訓與研究，具有豐富的專業實踐和教學經驗。參與多項重要文獻修復項目，代表性修復作品包括明萬曆《佛說當來彌勒出細寶卷》、清光緒《明聖經文》等。主持國家民委科研項目和教育部人文社會科學研究項目，在古籍保護、文博及材料科學等領域的國內外核心期刊發表學術論文十餘篇，申請發明專利五項。參與紙漿修復及貝葉刻抄本保護修復相關技術標準的制定，參與「古籍修復的理論與實踐」、「貝葉文獻保護修復」等課程教學及碩士研究生課題指導工作。

MoCC Anniversary Plenary Lecture: ‘Facing the New, Hot World’ 賽馬會氣候變化博物館周年傑出學者講座：「面對酷熱新世界」 - Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
From: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (MoCC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mocc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
賽馬會氣候變化博物館周年傑出學者講座：「面對酷熱新世界」
近年全球屢創高溫紀錄，極端天氣事件愈趨頻繁，這是否意味著我們對「氣候變化」的既有認知正在被顛覆？我們是否已接近某個臨界點，氣候即將進入人類從未經歷過的全新「酷熱時代」？媒體經常提及的「超級厄爾尼諾（Super El Niño）」又會否令世界變得更難以居住？面對日益嚴峻的氣候挑戰，我們又該如何應對未來的未知變局？
中大賽馬會氣候變化博物館（MoCC）於2013年成立，是全球首間以氣候變化為主題的博物館，自開館以來，透過多元渠道推動氣候教育與行動，累計參與人次超過二百萬。為迎接MoCC十三周年 ，我們非常榮幸邀請到前香港天文台台長林超英先生擔任演講嘉賓，並邀得香港中文大學偉倫地理及資源管理學系林紹顏教授擔任座談會嘉賓，以及MoCC學人劉霆鋒先生擔任主持，共同參與 MoCC周年傑出學者講座，三位嘉賓將會分享及探討全球氣候發展的最新趨勢，以及人類如何應對日益嚴峻的氣候挑戰，共同面對這個酷熱新世界
日期：2026年12月5日（星期六）
時間：上午10:00 – 11:30
地點：香港中文大學信和樓3樓李冠春堂（LKC LT1）
語言：廣東話
詳情及報名：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/.../2026/1460-mocc13-apl-ch
MoCC Anniversary Plenary Lecture: ‘Facing the New, Hot World’
In recent years, the world has witnessed record-breaking temperatures and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. Happenings are disrupting our established perception of ‘climate change’. Are we reaching a tipping point such that climate would transition into a new HOT regime which Homo sapiens has never experienced before? The media keeps talking about a Super El Niño, will it make the world ever less habitable? How do we prepare for the onslaught of extreme events?
The MoCC is the world’s first museum dedicated to the theme of climate change. Established in December 2013, the MoCC has accumulated over two million engagements through diverse climate education and action initiatives. To celebrate its 13th anniversary, we are honoured to have Mr Lam Chiu-ying, former Director of the Hong Kong Observatory, as our guest speaker. We are also delighted to have Professor Nina Lam Siu-ngan, Wei Lun Professor of Geography and Resources Management at CUHK, as our discussion panellist, and Mr Toby Lau, MoCC Scholar, as the moderator of the event. They will share and explore the latest developments in the global climate system, and discuss how we can adapt and build resilience in the face of the new, hot world
Date: 5 December 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 10:00 – 11:30 am
Venue: Li Koon Chun Hall (LKC LT1), Sino Building 3/F, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Language: Cantonese

中大賽馬會氣候變化博物館（MoCC）於2013年成立，是全球首間以氣候變化為主題的博物館，自開館以來，透過多元渠道推動氣候教育與行動，累計參與人次超過二百萬。為迎接MoCC十三周年 ，我們非常榮幸邀請到前香港天文台台長林超英先生擔任演講嘉賓，並邀得香港中文大學偉倫地理及資源管理學系林紹顏教授擔任座談會嘉賓，以及MoCC學人劉霆鋒先生擔任主持，共同參與 MoCC周年傑出學者講座，三位嘉賓將會分享及探討全球氣候發展的最新趨勢，以及人類如何應對日益嚴峻的氣候挑戰，共同面對這個酷熱新世界
日期：2026年12月5日（星期六）
時間：上午10:00 – 11:30
地點：香港中文大學信和樓3樓李冠春堂（LKC LT1）
語言：廣東話
詳情及報名：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/.../2026/1460-mocc13-apl-ch
MoCC Anniversary Plenary Lecture: ‘Facing the New, Hot World’
In recent years, the world has witnessed record-breaking temperatures and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. Happenings are disrupting our established perception of ‘climate change’. Are we reaching a tipping point such that climate would transition into a new HOT regime which Homo sapiens has never experienced before? The media keeps talking about a Super El Niño, will it make the world ever less habitable? How do we prepare for the onslaught of extreme events?
The MoCC is the world’s first museum dedicated to the theme of climate change. Established in December 2013, the MoCC has accumulated over two million engagements through diverse climate education and action initiatives. To celebrate its 13th anniversary, we are honoured to have Mr Lam Chiu-ying, former Director of the Hong Kong Observatory, as our guest speaker. We are also delighted to have Professor Nina Lam Siu-ngan, Wei Lun Professor of Geography and Resources Management at CUHK, as our discussion panellist, and Mr Toby Lau, MoCC Scholar, as the moderator of the event. They will share and explore the latest developments in the global climate system, and discuss how we can adapt and build resilience in the face of the new, hot world
Date: 5 December 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 10:00 – 11:30 am
Venue: Li Koon Chun Hall (LKC LT1), Sino Building 3/F, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Language: Cantonese

Dear Students,
What makes a language classroom experience positive and predictable? We would love to hear your thoughts!
The LEaPP Lab at the Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), invites you to participate in a research study exploring university students' experiences of language teaching and learning.
Who Can Participate?
Aged 18 or above;
Currently learning a second/foreign language in the formal classroom setting
What Does Participation Involve?
Complete an online questionnaire, which will take approximately
15–20 minutes
.

Participation Reward: HK$200 E-Gift Card!
Participants whose responses meet the study's data quality requirements will be eligible to enter a lucky draw for a
HK$200 e-gift card
.
After data collection has ended, selected winners will be contacted by email to receive their e-gift cards.

Ready to share your experience?

.

Announcements
HK$220 Stipend: Spoken Interaction fNIRS Experiment for Mandarin **MALE** Native Speakers (Approx. 2.5 Hours)  - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Xiaohui RAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
想了解语音互动过程中大脑如何活动吗？欢迎参加我们的无创脑成像研究，在获得实验报酬的同时体验前沿认知科学研究！
本实验室使用安全、无创的功能性近红外光谱（fNIRS）系统记录大脑血氧变化。该设备不会对人体造成伤害。如有任何安全顾虑，欢迎联系研究人员了解详情：Miss RAO，1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk。
实验内容及时间：
本研究为语音互动实验。参与者将佩戴安全、无创的功能性近红外光谱（fNIRS）设备进行实验，并填写问卷。实验总时长约2小时，其他准备工作0.5小时。被试费为220港元。
实验地点：中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。 实验结束后，会通过转数快支付被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求：
男性
年龄为18至30岁。
母语为汉语普通话。
听力正常。
无脑损伤、癫痫等神经系统疾病，无身体残疾，且无头皮外伤或感染。
右利手（写字，用筷子等习惯使用右手）。
没有参加过此实验的相关实验。如果不确定可以联系主试确认：Miss RAO,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
。
报名链接：
https://forms.gle/CZu7G4R58tiKjZop9
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
如有问题，请联系王女士（yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk）
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
English Version:
Interested in how the brain responds during spoken interaction? Join our non-invasive brain-imaging study, receive compensation, and experience current research in cognitive science!
This laboratory uses a safe, non-invasive functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) system to record changes in cerebral blood oxygenation. The procedure does not harm participants. If you have any safety concerns, please contact the researcher for further information: Miss RAO, 1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk.
Experiment Content & Duration:
This is a spoken-interaction experiment. Participants will wear a safe, non-invasive functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) device during the experiment and complete questionnaires. The total duration is approximately 2.5 hours, and the participation fee is HK$220.
Experiment location: Room G34, G/F, K.K. Leung Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong. The subject fee will be paid via FPS at the end of the experiment.
Participants need to meet the following requirements:
Male
Aged 18-30 years.
Native Mandarin Chinese speaker.
Have normal hearing.
No brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological disorders, and no scalp injury or infection.
Right-handed (writing, using chopsticks, etc.).
Have not participated in the preparatory experiment for this experiment. If you are not sure, you can contact the experimenter to confirm: Miss RAO, 1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk.
Link:
https://forms.gle/CZu7G4R58tiKjZop9
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact Miss Wang (yitingwang@cuhk.edu.hk)
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

How can we leverage AI to enhance student-staff partnerships in higher education?
I am thrilled to invite you and your network to our upcoming Student-Staff Partnership x AI Integration in Higher Education Seminar Series!
Join us as faculty members and their student partners share their real-world experiences and experiments with AI. We'll be exploring how co-creative approaches can enrich teaching and learning and reflecting on the essential knowledge, tools, and collaborative mindsets needed to navigate our rapidly evolving, AI-enhanced educational landscape.
Dates: 25 Nov | 14 Dec 2026
Time: 1:00 pm – 2:00 pm (UTC+8)
Venue: Online via Zoom
Whether you are an educator, a student, or simply passionate about the future of EdTech, the conversation is perfect for you.

APPLY NOW!!!MSc in Real Estate Programme (2027 intake)

MSc in Real Estate (MRE) is the only master’s degree in Asia that draws on multi-disciplinal research and teaching resources ranging from real estate, business to hospitality.
The programme offers an experiential learning curriculum that integrates theory and real-world practice to ensure that students understand multiple phases of the real estate development from business, investment and community perspectives.
Graduates of our programme will find career opportunities in areas such as development planning, research and consultancy, valuation, real estate finance, investment and management.
The programme is professionally accredited by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS). Graduates are eligible to become chartered surveyors with only 2 years of relevant professional experience, compared with 5 or more years for non-accredited degree holders.

Apply NOW

香港中文大學商學院房地産理學碩士課程是亞洲唯一融合房地産、商業和旅遊資産學科研究和教學資源的碩士課程。
課程結合理論與行業實踐，透過體驗式學習，從商業投資和社區角度教授學生房地産不同發展階段的知識與技能。

課程獲皇家特許測量師學會認証，畢業生於相關領域工作2年後可申請成爲全球認可的注冊測量師（非認証課程畢業生需要最少5年）。

New Insomnia Intervention Study Recruiting Participants  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Chen Yang, Chris Xie Chen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155249610@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【聲音刺激增強慢波睡眠改善失眠患者睡眠品質的初步實驗研究】
參加者
招募

香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究室正進行一項初步實驗研究，測試聲音刺激是否可以改善失眠症患者的睡眠品質。
研究對象：
18至45歲成年人
確診現在患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
没有确诊的精神疾患，如精神分裂症，分裂性情感障碍等。
研究
內容
:
佩戴14天體動手錶、填寫睡眠日記。
配戴手錶期間挑選一日於上午前往公立醫院睡眠研究室，進行全日檢測（認知測試、情緒睡眠評估、問卷填寫）, 並接受全夜多導睡眠檢查，檢查費用全免。
地點：新界沙田醫院，7樓A病房 – 睡眠檢查室
你可能會在深度睡眠期接受低頻聲音刺激。
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $600 的購物禮券津貼。名額有限，先到先得！如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下連結報名，我們將在兩個工作日以內聯繫符合條件的報名者，謝謝。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電或whatsapp 59322728與負責研究人員聯絡，查詢詳情。
【
A pilot experimental study of acoustic stimulation in enhancing slow wave sleep to improve sleep quality in insomnia disorder
】
The Li Chiu Kong Family Sleep Assessment Unit of the Department of Psychiatry is conducting a pilot study to examine whether acoustic stimulation could improve sleep quality in patients with insomnia disorder.
Eligibility criteria:
Adults aged 18 to 45 years old
With diagnosed insomnia disorder (i.e., having insomnia symptoms at least 3 times per week, lasting for at least 3 months, with daytime function impairment)
No diagnosed psychiatric disorder, such as schizophrenia
Measurements:
14-day actigraphy and sleep diary document
One full day assessment in sleep assessment unit (cognitive assessments, clinical interview, online questionnaires..)
One overnight polysomnography
Location:Sleep Assessment Unit,7A,Shatin Hospital,NT
You may receive binaural acoustic stimulation during deep sleep.
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $600.
Limited quota- first come firs served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact: 59322728

地點：新界沙田醫院，7樓A病房 – 睡眠檢查室
你可能會在深度睡眠期接受低頻聲音刺激。
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $600 的購物禮券津貼。名額有限，先到先得！如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下連結報名，我們將在兩個工作日以內聯繫符合條件的報名者，謝謝。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電或whatsapp 59322728與負責研究人員聯絡，查詢詳情。
【
A pilot experimental study of acoustic stimulation in enhancing slow wave sleep to improve sleep quality in insomnia disorder
】
The Li Chiu Kong Family Sleep Assessment Unit of the Department of Psychiatry is conducting a pilot study to examine whether acoustic stimulation could improve sleep quality in patients with insomnia disorder.
Eligibility criteria:
Adults aged 18 to 45 years old
With diagnosed insomnia disorder (i.e., having insomnia symptoms at least 3 times per week, lasting for at least 3 months, with daytime function impairment)
No diagnosed psychiatric disorder, such as schizophrenia
Measurements:
14-day actigraphy and sleep diary document
One full day assessment in sleep assessment unit (cognitive assessments, clinical interview, online questionnaires..)
One overnight polysomnography
Location:Sleep Assessment Unit,7A,Shatin Hospital,NT
You may receive binaural acoustic stimulation during deep sleep.
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $600.
Limited quota- first come firs served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact: 59322728

香港中文大学语言加工实验室现招募志愿者参加一项关于中文句子理解的行为实验。任务简单，欢迎报名参加！
**实验内容：**参与者将在电脑上阅读普通话句子，并根据第一直觉从图片中选择最符合句子内容的物品。

**实验地点：**香港中文大学梁銶琚楼G层G34实验室（语言学及现代语言系）。

年龄在18至30岁之间；
来自中国大陆，以普通话为母语；
非心理学专业。

Approximately 15–20 minutes.

Startup Meetup @InnoPort | CUAEA × CUHK InnoPort - FlyTaxi: Local Startup Survival & Exit Playbook
Facing well-funded multinational giants and fierce price-slashing competition, how can a homegrown tech platform carve out its own path and thrive? From scaling from scratch to over a million users, all the way to securing a strategic buyout offer from a competitor—what does it truly take to survive, scale, and exit in the local startup landscape?
CUHK InnoPort and CUHK Alumni Entrepreneurs Association (CUAEA) proudly present the next session of the Startup Meetup @ InnoPort series (初創聚一聚系列)! We are thrilled to feature CUHK alumnus Simon Siu, Founder of the prominent local ride-hailing platform FlyTaxi. Through an intimate Fireside Chat, Simon will break down the realities of his decade-long entrepreneurial journey, daily crisis-management ("firefighting") experiences, agile product tactics, and how hyper-local insights positioned FlyTaxi for a successful acquisition.
Event Highlights
Battle-tested startup strategies: How a local tech platform navigated deep-pocketed competitors and price wars using agile execution and deep local market insights
Candid alumni insights: Real stories behind a decade of entrepreneurial challenges, day-to-day crises, and the playbook for attracting an acquisition offer
Cross-sector networking: Connect with CUHK students, alumni, founders, and industry professionals to exchange insights and explore collaborations

免費參加！各位中大校友同創業家留意喇！ 面對過江龍大財團嘅「燒錢戰」，本地初創點樣可以殺出一條血路？
CUHK InnoPort
@cuhkinnoport
同 CUAEA 聯手舉辦嘅「初創聚一聚 @ InnoPort」系列嚟喇！今次我哋好榮幸請到本地知名叫車平台「飛的」創辦人兼中大校友 Simon，親自分享佢點樣將「飛的」由零做起，累積過百萬用戶，最後仲成功吸引對手出價收購嘅傳奇實戰故事！
如果你都喺創業路上奮鬥緊，或者對 Startup 點樣突圍、賣盤（Exit）有興趣，就絕對唔可以錯過今次嘅 Fireside Chat！現場仲有輕食提供，放工過嚟 chill 住傾、識下朋友啦！
活動三大亮點：
創業實戰交流｜無懼跨國巨頭競爭！探討本地科技平台點樣憑住敏捷打法同最貼地嘅本土 insight，由零突圍並持續成長！
中大校友深度經驗談｜Fireside Chat 零距離交流！由 Simon 親述創業十幾年嚟嘅真實挑戰同「救火」日常，獨家分享吸引對手買盤嘅終極攻略！
建立跨界連繫｜同中大同學、校友、創業團隊及各界專業人士交流，拓展跨界別人脈，互相交流取經！
活動詳情：
日期：2026 年 11 月 20 日（星期五）
⏰ 時間：晚上 7:00 - 9:00
地點：UGA 活動廳, InnoPort
語言：粵語
費用：全免
備註：提供輕食及飲料
講者：
Mr. Simon SIU 蕭達文｜「飛的」創辦人
（Simon 帶領團隊憑藉靈活策略同精準洞察，成功將平台打造成服務逾百萬用戶嘅本地旗艦，累積極具參考價值嘅初創實戰及退場經驗！）
主持：
Ms. Cleopatra TAM｜中大創業校友會．教育事務委員會副主席
Ms. Christine LEUNG｜香港中文大學創博館．經理

bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/11/13
»
Announcements
( Receive up to HK$400Allowance!) Recruiting young adults (aged 18–24)for online sleep and mental health intervention with individualized support （最高可獲得$400津貼！）誠邀18至24歲青年參加網上睡眠及心理健康課程，仲有個人化的指導 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What will you do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/11/13
»
Announcements
‼We sincerely invite individuals experiencing symptoms of depression or anxiety to join an online mental health self-care journey research study 【Up to HK$400 Voucher 】‼ ‼誠邀正經歷抑鬱或焦慮症狀的人士參與網上心理健康自我照顧旅程研究【最高可獲$400現金卷】‼ - Department of Psychology
From: Charles Kwun
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
charleskwun@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(Please scroll down for English version)
網上個人化心理健康自我照顧旅程研究
參加者招募
不知道有什麼工具能夠幫助自己在情緒低落時，好好照顧自己心理健康？
我們誠邀你參加網上個人化心理健康自我照顧旅程研究。是次研究旨在評估與院校恆常服務相比，網上心理健康平台對香港初顯期成人（emerging adults）在處理心理困擾及培養自我照顧的成效 。
立即報名（約 5 分鐘填寫篩選問卷）：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_5uTpLpl9UZNfAvs
我們正在招募能夠滿足以下條件的參加者：
年齡介乎18至29歲
能閱讀及理解中文/廣東話
有智能手機、平板電腦或電腦，可定期上網並能出席Zoom
正經歷抑鬱或焦慮症狀，且困擾持續2個月。（由研究人員篩選評估）
從未註冊或登入賽馬會心導遊+
平台 JCTH+ 次數不多於兩次的現有會員
實驗流程：
登記報名並完成篩選問卷，以確認參加資格*
合資格的參加者會被隨機分配至實驗組和常規治療對照組。
實驗組參加者需要參加六週有指導的網上自我照顧介入，而對照組則繼續使用常規的心理健康服務。
期間兩組均需要完成基線問卷、課後（第6週）問卷及4份跟進問卷（1份詳細問卷，及3份簡單問卷）。
答謝金：
為答謝你所付出的時間，在研究完成後你最高可獲得總值港幣400元現金券#！
* 名額有限，若果報名人數過多，將會隨機抽取部分合資格人士參與研究 ,問卷將透過電郵發送，並需要在收到後的四日內完成。
# 通過有效性檢測後，現金券會分兩次在完成第六週問卷及全部跟進問卷後兩個月內派發。詳情請參閱知情同意書。
如對是項研究有任何疑問，歡迎電郵至本計劃的研究人員官先生(
charleskwun@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或湯博士 (alantong@cuhk.edu.hk)聯絡。如對研究參與者的權利有任何查詢，請聯絡香港中文大學調查及行為研究操守委員會 (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk)。
本研究已獲得香港中文大學調查及行為研究倫理委員會 (編號SBRE-25-1031)
Online Personalized Mental Health Self-Care Journey Study
Recruiting Participants
Not sure what tools can help you take good care of your mental health when you’re feeling low?
We sincerely invite you to join our Online Personalized Mental Health Self-Care Journey Study. This study aims to evaluate an online mental health platform on promoting mental health self-care and managing psychological distress among emerging adults in Hong Kong, compared to a treatment-as-usual control group.
Register now (the screening questionnaire takes approximately 5 minutes):
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_5uTpLpl9UZNfAvs
We are recruiting participants who meet the following criteria:
Aged 18 to 29
Able to read and understand Chinese / Cantonese
Have a smartphone, tablet or computer with regular internet access and are able to attend Zoom sessions
Experiencing symptoms of depression or anxiety, lasting for 2 months or more (to be screened and assessed by researchers)
Have not previously registered for the Jockey Club TourHeart+ platform OR an existing member with 2 or fewer log-ins.
What will you have to do
Complete a screening questionnaire to check for eligibility*
Eligible participants will be randomly distributed to experimental or control condition.
Participants in the experimental group will take part in a 6-week guided digital self-care intervention, while those in the control group will continue using their usual mental health services.
Participants in both groups will complete a baseline questionnaire, a post (Week 6) questionnaire, and 4 follow-up questionnaires (1 long + 3 short questionnaires)
Compensation:
As a token of appreciation for your time, you can receive up to a maximum of HKD400 in cash vouchers upon completion of the study#!
* Due to limited availability, if the number of registrations exceeds the capacity, a random selection of eligible individuals will be made. The questionnaire will be sent via email and need to be completed within four days of receiving it.
# After passing validity checks, cash vouchers will be distributed within 2 months after completion of the Post questionnaire and after completion of all follow-up questionnaires. See terms and condition in the consent form。
For any inquiries, please contact the research assistant, Mr. Charles Kwun (
charleskwun@cuhk.edu.hk
), or Research Assistant Professor, Dr. Alan Tong (
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
). Should you have any enquires about the rights of research participants, please contact The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics (
fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk
).
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee of CUHK (Reference No.: SBRE-25-1031).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Invitation to YANG Jinbai's Chinese Painting Solo Exhibition 誠邀參加《鑿山 -- 楊近白國畫展》 - Lee Woo Sing College
From: Lee Woo Sing College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wscollege@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(Scroll down for English version)
[鑿山--楊近白國畫展 | YANG Jinbai’s Chinese Painting Solo Exhibition]
楊近白先生從書法跨足國畫，用沉著筆觸勾出山水間宏偉莊觀，全面展現個人風格及當代中國傳統藝術的新面向。是次國畫展由和聲書院副輔導長萬超教授策展，書院亦邀請楊近白先生於11月20日開幕禮到場，即席分享技法心得、導覧展出作品以及現場示範國畫創作。
《鑿山--楊近白國畫展》
展期：2026年11月20日至2026年12月14日
地點：和聲書院低層一樓展覧走廊
開幕禮及導賞 (普通話)：2026年11月20日；中午12時至中午12時45分
現場國畫示範 (普通話)：2026年11月20日；下午2時30分至下午4時30分
如欲報名參加開幕禮、導賞或現場國畫示範，請提交Webform至
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13717268
。
Transitioning from calligraphy to Chinese painting, Mr. YANG Jinbai uses composed brushstrokes to outline the magnificent and grand landscapes between mountains, fully showcasing his personal style and new dimensions in contemporary Chinese traditional art. Lee Woo Sing College is hosting Mr. YANG’s calligraphy and painting solo exhibition, curated by Professor WAN Chao, Associate Dean of Students of the College. The College has also invited Mr. YANG to attend the opening ceremony on November 20 to share insights on his techniques, guide a tour of the exhibited works, and conduct a live demonstration of calligraphy and painting.
"Y
ANG Jinbai’s Chinese Painting Solo Exhibition”

Nov 20, 2026 – Dec 14, 2026
Venue:
LG1 Exhibition Corridor, Lee Woo Sing College

anguage: Putonghua)

.

title: The Politics of Cute
bodyText:

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Politics of Cute  - Department of Cultural and Religious Studies
From: FAN SIXIN
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cyxinfan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
From the global expansion of Sanrio fandom to the rise of social capital around Labubu and Jellycat, and the ways K-Pop stars, real or animated, and cute animals, like the quokka and Fennec fox, have taken the world by storm, cuteness is a twenty-first-century sensation. This conference explores a “cuteness turn” found in many public realms around the world. The adoration of attractive or cheerful objects associated with childishness and youthfulness is part of the human experience. However, this conference does not examine cuteness as a transcultural aesthetic or psychological condition, but we focus on its larger political implications. Throughout history and around the world, this “universal” sentiment has often been manipulated for commercial and ideological purposes. This conference focuses on the political use of cuteness in social movements, political propaganda, public lobbying, and campaigns for public office, among other contexts, a phenomenon occurring at the intersection of popular culture and political participation.
While many consider cuteness a reflection of the “infantilization” or “feminization” of the adorers, we need more careful analysis to understand the elaborate calculation, personal expressions, and manifestation of bonding behind many of the related phenomena. There could be many commercial and political interests involved, but the producers and users also appropriate these objects or images for self-empowerment. This conference studies how cuteness is situated in the intersection between the public and the private, the political and the social. The production, consumption, and distribution of cute objects and images could be commercially driven, but the usages and exhibitions of these objects and images could also be staged as a collective protest against the established world of the adult. These cute objects might be a strategic result of political negotiation, and they might also reflect a complex entanglement between public formation and subject formation. These objects form a unique nodal point where the public and private meet, reminding us how the public is constructed and manifested in many forms.

便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼

下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數

階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:

We are delighted to invite you to participate in our
upcoming career networking session
, which aims to connect CUHK ventures with experienced business professionals!
Who are we looking for?
Tech Ventures
: CUHK-related technology ventures seeking C-level executives, business leaders, advisors, mentors, or other professional talent to support their business development and growth.

⭐⭐⭐Parent and Child Participants Needed (Twins and Singletons)! Maximum $550 allowance and a performance report! 誠邀家長和小朋友(包括單生兒和雙胞胎)參與研究！最高可獲得共$550報酬和個人報告！⭐⭐⭐  - Department of Psychology
From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15
分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
*
現在報名的幼稚園高班至六年級學童只需完成今年一次測試
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：今年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
is reshaping how humans learn, work, create, communicate, and make decisions. This course examines the ethical, social, and governance challenges posed by AI through a human-centred lens.
Students will explore how AI affects higher education, professional practice, public institutions, and society at large, investigating issues such as authenticity, academic integrity, fairness, accountability, transparency, human agency, and democratic governance. The course culminates in an exploration of responsible human-AI relations and governance approaches that promote human flourishing, dignity, and societal well-being in an AI-enabled future.
Topics:
Human and AI: Foundations of Intelligence, Agency, and Personhood
AI Ethics
AI Governance and Future Challenges
Human-AI Relations: Moral Status, Rights, and Future Coexistence
Units:
2 (interactive lectures with discussions and activities)
Language of instruction:
English
Course enrolment:
Offered in Term 2, 2026–27. Open to all students except
Artificial Intelligence: Systems and Technologies
majors. Students must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in UGFH1000 or UGFN1000.

The new
UGFN1002
In Dialogue with
Nature
is a 2-unit version of UGFN1000. It will be offered as a pilot offering in Term 2, 2026-27, with a full launch in 2027-28.
SAME BIG QUESTIONS
READ · QUESTION · DISCUSS · REFLECT
Students will continue to explore the fundamental and enduring issues arising from human interactions with the natural world, including:
How do humans approach nature?
What understanding have humans gained through interacting with nature?
How does such understanding affect values, and how is it influenced by values?
SIX CLASSIC TEXTS
We will explore these enduring questions through six classic texts:
Republic
,
The Principia: Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy
,
On the Origin of Species
,
In Search of Memory: The Emergence of a New Science of Mind
,
The Shorter Science and Civilisation
in China: An Abridgement of Joseph Needham’s Original Text
. Vol. 1,
A Sand County Almanac and Sketches Here and There
.
Through lectures and small-group tutorials, students exchange ideas and perspectives and engage in meaningful dialogue.
A NEW CLASS ARRANGEMENT
Classes follow a biweekly cycle, with a two-hour lecture and a two-hour tutorial held in alternate weeks.
Course enrolment:
Four English-medium class sections will be offered in Term 2, 2026-27.
UGFN1002 is not open to students who have previously completed UGFN1000 or UGFN1001.
Note for students admitted in 2026–27 or earlier:
Effective 2027–28, the existing 3-unit UGFN1000 course will be replaced with the 2-unit version. Students who have not completed the required 3-unit GE Foundation course(s) by the end of 2026–27 will need to complete the corresponding 2-unit course(s) and make up the remaining unit(s) through additional unit(s) from the GE Four-Area curriculum. The same make-up requirement also applies to students taking the 2-unit pilot courses in Term 2, 2026–27.

The new
UGFH1002
In Dialogue with Humanity
is a 2-unit version of UGFH1000. It will be offered as a pilot offering in Term 2, 2026-27, with a full launch in 2027-28.
SAME BIG QUESTIONS
READ · QUESTION · DISCUSS · REFLECT
Students will continue to engage with three fundamental questions:
What are the potentials of human beings?
What is it that makes a good life for an individual?
What is it that makes a good society for the community?
SIX CLASSIC TEXTS
We will explore these enduring questions through six classic texts:
The Odyssey, The Analects, The Heart Sutra, The Bible, The Social Contract, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844.
Through lectures and small-group tutorials, students exchange ideas and perspectives and engage in meaningful dialogue.
A NEW CLASS ARRANGEMENT
Classes follow a biweekly cycle, with a two-hour lecture and a two-hour tutorial held in alternate weeks.
Course enrolment:
Four English-medium class sections will be offered in Term 2, 2026-27.
UGFH1002 is not open to students who have previously completed UGFH1000 or UGFH1001.
Note for students admitted in 2026–27 or earlier:
Effective 2027–28, the existing 3-unit UGFH1000 course will be replaced with the 2-unit version. Students who have not completed the required 3-unit GE Foundation course(s) by the end of 2026–27 will need to complete the corresponding 2-unit course(s) and make up the remaining unit(s) through additional unit(s) from the GE Four-Area curriculum. The same make-up requirement also applies to students taking the 2-unit pilot courses in Term 2, 2026–27.

(The application below is conducted in Chinese only.)
日期：2026年11月20日（星期五）
時間：下午12時半至2時
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓5樓505室
語言：廣東話
講者：黃憬珩先生（香港藝穗會顧問）
免費登記：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13745553
講者簡介：
黃憬珩先生，香港藝穗會顧問、書畫藝術家、古董收藏家及藝術策展人。出身香港收藏之家，師承「小楷王」何幼惠老師及盧清遠老師，作品獲私人收藏家及香港大學等多所機構收藏。黃憬珩從事書畫創作、策展與公眾教育，透過收藏鑑賞、文化講座及藝術教育，引領大眾走近中國書畫與傳統文化，曾於香港浸會大學舉辦收藏展及講座，並於多個國家及地區策劃展覽。
講座簡介：
黃氏家族的收藏傳承綿延五代。縱使藏品在時代變遷中幾經散聚，對文物的熱愛卻始終薪火相傳。黃憬珩將分享家族與個人的收藏故事，並透過書畫與典籍收藏實物，引領大眾認識香港近代文人的收藏風尚。講座亦會談及北山堂、學海書樓、至樂樓等影響香港近代文化甚深的組織與藏家傳奇，共同探尋百年文脈與文人情懷在當代的生命力。

M.A. in Global Communication 20th Anniversary International Symposium – Possible AI Futures: Situating Global Communication in an Unsettled World
As the M.A. in Global Communication programme marks the milestone of its 20th anniversary, the two-day symposium brings together international scholars and practitioners for a timely conversation on AI futures and the worlds they are helping to shape. The anniversary is both a moment to reflect on the programme’s history and an opportunity to consider what global communication now demands of us in an age when AI is reshaping institutions, publics, knowledge production, and everyday life.

The Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages at CUHK cordially invites you to join our Modern Languages courses from our Minor Programmes in the Term 2 of 2026-27.

title: 【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/11/13
»
Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study  誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀3歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 33個月或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿3歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on the gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between the gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is under 33 months old (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 3 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

bodyText:

»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The RISE Dialogue: Navigating Academic Challenges with Resilience and Integrity  - Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research
From: Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
carmenlau@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear colleagues and students,
We would like to invite you to join the first session of the series brought to you by the TDLEG-IICA project
“Resilience and Integrity through Scenario-based Engagement (RISE)”
, a collaborative initiative among thirteen partner institutions.
Workshop Title:
The RISE Dialogue: Navigating Academic Challenges with Resilience and Integrity
Date:
November 18, 2026
Time:
11:00 am – 12:30 pm
Venue:
JC3 302-303, Jockey Club Campus of Creativity, Hong Kong Baptist University (
Map
)
Facilitator:
Dr Kristen LI, Senior Lecturer, Department of Computer Science, HKBU
Panellists:
Dr Paolo MENGONI, Senior Lecturer, Department of Interactive Media, HKBU
Mr Sebastian PAHS, Lecturer, Academy of Geography, Sociology and International Studies, HKBU
Prof Pak Hang WONG, Assistant Professor, Academy of Chinese, History, Religion and Philosophy, HKBU
Abstract:
How do we thrive amidst rapid technological change and high-stress academic life? Success today is about building inner strength to overcome setbacks and having a strong ethical foundation to guide our actions.  This panel brings together faculty members across disciplines to share their insights, strategies, and innovative practices for fostering resilience and integrity in education.
Join us for the inaugural workshop of the RISE project and be part of this important conversation. Please see the
poster
for more details. All are welcome!

"Investor and Financial Education for All: Don't Freestyle Your Investments!"
/
「投資理財人人都要識︰投資切忌 Freestyle!」
.

Earn up to $130 for an email task and an interview! You are invited to participate in a study on university student's email language practice in Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales at the Department of English.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to understand how university students communicate with their instructors through email in their everyday lives, and what experiences and social contexts may influence their email-writing practices.
Eligibility
All university students currently enrolled in a university in Hong Kong is eligible to join.
Research Procedure
Participation in this study involves the following two parts:
Completing an English email-writing task; and
Completing a short questionnaire in English.
The entire process will take approximately
15 to 20 minutes
.
Some participants may be invited to take part in an individual follow-up interview. The interview will explore participants’ email-writing choices, their everyday email-writing practices, and the educational, work-related, online, and other social experiences that may be associated with these practices.
Compensation
Participants who complete the email-writing task will receive
HK$30
as compensation.
Participants who are invited to and complete a follow-up interview will receive an additional
HK$100
as compensation.
To Participate
If you are interested, please complete the short email task and a questionnaire via the link below:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3PYFjhsYB6M5nca
Confidentiality and Consent
All responses will be kept strictly confidential. You will be asked to provide your name and email address. These are collected only for administrative purposes (e.g., tracking participation). You may withdraw from the study at any time without penalty.
Ethics Approval
SBRE-25-0524A: Email-Writing Profiles and Their Social Contexts: An Exploratory Study of Student–Instructor Email Communication

title: Win a HKD$100 Gift Card in Prize Draw!! Recruiting CUHK Undergraduate Students (Aged 18–25) for a Study on Anxiety and Independent Life Skills!!! （可參加抽獎贏取港幣 $100 禮品卡！）誠邀中大本科生（18–25 歲）參與焦慮與獨立生活技能之關聯研究！
bodyText:
